lessons.title: Origins — Blind Prodigy, Detroit, & Motown Training

body.text: Training Goals: Teach the foundation of genius. “How does a kid control a crowd like that?”

body.label: Key points
items: Self-taught on multiple instruments by age 8
“Little Stevie Wonder” era → child prodigy on harmonica & drums
Mentorship from Berry Gordy, Marvin Gaye, Smokey Robinson

lessons.title: The Teenage Artist — Voice Developing, Identity Forming

body.text: Identity Forming Goals: Understand his transition from prodigy to artist. Lesson: “Even geniuses need YEARS of practice.”

body.label: Key points
items: Puberty shifted his voice → deeper tone
Motown putting him in different styles (pop, R&B, standards)

lessons.title: The Classic Period Begins — Music of My Mind

body.text: Mind Goals: Teach the moment Stevie seized artistic control. Break down how “Superwoman” is TWO songs woven into one.

body.label: Key points
items: 1971 contract renegotiation — Stevie gained FULL artistic control
He begins playing most instruments himself
Part of what we call “Stevie’s Classic Period”
“Superwoman (Where Were You When I Needed You)”

body.text: Innovation Goals: Teach how Stevie rewrote pop and R&B. Have your son listen to just the CLAVINET on “Superstition.” Teach him how one instrument can carry a whole vibe.

body.label: Key points
items: Fusion of synths, clavinet, funk rhythm
The birth of his “message + groove” formula
“You Are the Sunshine of My Life”

body.text: as Literature Goals: Teach political-songwriting. Break down “Living for the City” like a STORY — characters, plot, conflict, theme. Your son gon’ learn literary analysis.

body.label: Key points

The album as a narrative experience
